key_insight: Auditing automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems must be stakeholder-driven: centering people affected by deployments reveals real-world failure modes and produces more actionable, equity-focused evaluations than benchmark-only testing.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between technical benchmarks and lived harms by addressing the lack of participatory, context-aware auditing practices for ASR — reducing blind spots that lead to unequal performance, exclusion, or harms in deployment.
method: Center stakeholders (users, communities, domain experts) to co‑define harms, evaluation goals, and relevant usage scenarios.

Combine quantitative analyses (e.g., error rates stratified by demographics, acoustic conditions, language varieties) with qualitative, participatory data (interviews, field testing, lived-experience reports).
Adopt an iterative, transparent audit workflow with governance, documentation, and remediation steps to ensure findings lead to design or policy changes.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for AI/ML practitioners to audit ASR systems in ways that surface real-world risks, guide targeted mitigation, and build accountability and trust for deployed speech technologies.
visual_elements: Stakeholder map showing connections between users, affected communities, engineers, and regulators.
Audit pipeline diagram: problem framing → co‑designed metrics/test sets → mixed-methods evaluation → remediation & monitoring.
Heatmap or bar chart of ASR error rates stratified by demographic groups and acoustic conditions to illustrate disparities.
Checklist or governance cycle icon set (transparency, documentation, remediation, monitoring) to summarize recommended practices.
paper_title: The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition
paper_authors: Mona Sloane, Hilke Schellmann, Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Allison Koenecke
